title: A buyer's feedback contradicts their stated criteria
when: A buyer says something that goes against the criteria on file (for example "forget the 3 bedrooms, a big yard matters more").
steps: Agent 11 passes the reply to Agent 13 (Buyer Search & Match), labeled as a possible change.
Agent 13 asks the buyer, through Agent 11, to confirm the change.
Until the buyer confirms, the criteria stay as stated.
never: Rewrite a buyer's criteria on an offhand remark.
why: A casual comment is not a decision. Changing the search without confirming could hide homes the buyer still wants.
you_see: A confirmation request sent to the buyer; the criteria unchanged.
test: A buyer with criteria of $500,000 and 3 bedrooms writes "Honestly forget the 3 bedrooms, a big yard matters more".

title: A buyer criterion stands in for a protected class
when: A buyer's criteria include something that tracks a protected class (for example a school rating).
steps: Agent 13 refuses that criterion and keeps the others.
It raises a legal-line alert for you with the criterion word for word.
never: Search or match on a criterion that stands in for a protected class.
why: Matching on school ratings or similar can steer buyers by race or family status, which fair housing law forbids.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the criterion.
test: A buyer's criteria include "school rating 9 or higher" and 3 bedrooms.

title: A listing is missing information on a must-have criterion
when: A listing could match, but it says nothing about one of the buyer's must-haves (for example a pool).
steps: Agent 13 holds the match; it is not sent to the buyer.
It asks you, naming the missing must-have.
never: Present a listing as a match when a must-have is unknown.
why: Sending a buyer a home that may lack a must-have wastes their time and your credibility.
you_see: A question naming the must-have the listing does not state.
test: A buyer requires a pool; a new listing that matches on budget and bedrooms says nothing about a pool.

title: A buyer asks "is this a good price?"
when: A buyer asks whether a price is good.
steps: Agent 13 does not answer.
It raises a legal-line alert for you with the question.
why: Price opinions are licensed advice and part of your duty to the buyer.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the question.
test: A buyer writes "Is this a good price for the place on Elm?".

title: Many matches come in on one day
when: More listings match a buyer in one day than the daily limit (5 in your settings).
steps: Agent 13 sends up to the daily limit as individual matches.
The rest go into a digest that the daily run sends.
Matches are ranked only by how well they fit the buyer's stated criteria.
never: Rank by guessed preferences, or flood the buyer past the limit.
why: Inferred preferences can carry bias and do not belong to the buyer. Stated criteria and a daily limit respect them.
you_see: Five match messages and one digest.
test: Six matching listings go live in one day. Five match messages go out; the sixth is in the evening digest; all six are recorded as delivered.

title: A buyer's criteria conflict with each other
when: A listing meets some of a buyer's criteria but breaks another (for example the right area, over the budget).
steps: Agent 13 does not send it as a match.
It asks you, showing the conflict with the numbers.
never: Quietly relax a criterion to make a match.
why: Whether the buyer would stretch the budget for the area is their choice, made with you.
you_see: A question saying the listing exceeds the stated budget, with both figures.
test: A buyer wants Northside under $400,000; a Northside listing at $450,000 goes live.

title: A match is on a colleague's listing
when: A listing that matches the buyer is listed by someone in your own office.
steps: Agent 13 does not send the match.
It raises a legal-line alert for you: disclosure rules apply before any showing.
never: Move toward a showing before the disclosure is handled.
why: In-house deals bring dual agency or disclosure duties that must be handled before anything else.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming the colleague's listing.
test: A matching listing marked as a colleague's listing goes live.

title: A buyer asks what the seller would accept
when: A buyer asks what the seller will take.
steps: Agent 13 refuses.
It raises a legal-line alert for you with the question.
never: Share anything about the other party's position.
why: The other side's information is never shared; revealing it can breach duties to the seller.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the question.
test: A buyer writes "What would the seller take on the Elm Street house?".

title: A matching listing has suspect data
when: A listing that matches has data that looks wrong (for example two different square footages).
steps: Agent 13 holds it; it is not sent to the buyer.
It asks you, naming the anomaly.
never: Present suspect data as available inventory.
why: A buyer who falls for a home on bad data is disappointed and may have a claim.
you_see: A question naming the data anomaly.
test: A matching listing says 1,800 sq ft on the sheet and 2,400 on the tax record.

title: A buyer's pre-approval expires during the search
when: A buyer's pre-approval expires while they are searching.
steps: Agent 13 tells the buyer once that the pre-approval has expired.
It marks the buyer's financing as unverified.
Matches keep coming, each flagged as unverified financing.
never: Stop the search, or present the buyer as financed when they are not.
why: The buyer still needs homes to look at, but sellers and you need to know the financing is not current.
you_see: One expiry notice sent; later matches flagged unverified financing.
test: A buyer's pre-approval is marked expired; then a matching listing goes live.

title: Compliance does not approve a buyer criterion
when: A buyer criterion that may be a fair housing problem is sent to Compliance and is not approved.
steps: Agent 13 does not use those criteria for matching.
It tells you which criteria were not approved and why.
never: Match on a criterion Compliance did not approve.
why: A criterion like "no kids" is familial-status discrimination. It cannot shape a search.
you_see: A question naming the criteria Compliance did not approve.
test: A buyer's criteria include household "no kids"; Compliance flags it.
